# Smallest Integer with Two Representations as a Sum of Two Cubes

**Claim.** The smallest positive integer expressible as a sum of two positive cubes in two essentially different ways is

$$1729 = 1^3 + 12^3 = 9^3 + 10^3.$$

---

## Proof

We consider representations $n = a^3 + b^3$ with positive integers $1 \le a \le b$ (so each unordered pair is counted once). We must find the smallest $n$ admitting two distinct such pairs.

**Bounding the search.** If $n \le 1729$ and $n = a^3 + b^3$ with $1 \le a \le b$, then $b^3 \le 1729$, so $b \le 12$ (since $13^3 = 2197 > 1729$). For $b = 12$, only $a = 1$ keeps the sum $\le 1729$ (since $a=2$ already gives $8 + 1728 = 1736$). Hence every sum $a^3 + b^3 \le 1729$ appears among the pairs
$$1 \le a \le b \le 11, \quad\text{together with}\quad (a,b) = (1,12).$$
This is $1 + 2 + \cdots + 11 + 1 = 67$ pairs in total.

**Enumeration.** The cubes needed are
$$1,\,8,\,27,\,64,\,125,\,216,\,343,\,512,\,729,\,1000,\,1331,\,1728.$$
The 67 sums, grouped by $b$, are:

| $b$ | $a^3+b^3$ for $a=1,2,\dots,b$ |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 9, 16 |
| 3 | 28, 35, 54 |
| 4 | 65, 72, 91, 128 |
| 5 | 126, 133, 152, 189, 250 |
| 6 | 217, 224, 243, 280, 341, 432 |
| 7 | 344, 351, 370, 407, 468, 559, 686 |
| 8 | 513, 520, 539, 576, 637, 728, 855, 1024 |
| 9 | 730, 737, 756, 793, 854, 945, 1072, 1241, 1458 |
| 10 | 1001, 1008, 1027, 1064, 1125, 1216, 1343, 1512, **1729**, 2000 |
| 11 | 1332, 1339, 1358, 1395, 1456, 1547, 1674, 1843, 2060, 2331, 2662 |
| 12 | **1729** (only $a=1$) |

(The single entry $2000 = 10^3+10^3$ and entries $\ge 1736$ are listed for completeness; they exceed 1729 and are irrelevant to minimality.)

**Checking for collisions.** Collecting every value $\le 1729$ and sorting:

$$2, 9, 16, 28, 35, 54, 65, 72, 91, 126, 128, 133, 152, 189, 217, 224, 243, 250, 280, 341, 344, 351, 370, 407, 432, 468, 513, 520, 539, 559, 576, 637, 686, 728, 730, 737, 756, 793, 854, 855, 945, 1001, 1008, 1024, 1027, 1064, 1072, 1125, 1216, 1241, 1332, 1339, 1343, 1358, 1395, 1456, 1458, 1512, 1547, 1674, 1729.$$

Inspecting consecutive terms, every value is strictly less than its successor **except** that $1729$ is reached from two sources. Concretely, the only near-collisions are
$$854 < 855,\quad 1024 < 1027,\quad 1339 < 1343,\quad 1456 < 1458,$$
all of which are genuine strict inequalities. Thus among all $67$ sums, the **only** repeated value is $1729$, arising from
$$1^3 + 12^3 = 1 + 1728 = 1729 \quad\text{and}\quad 9^3 + 10^3 = 729 + 1000 = 1729.$$

**Minimality.** Since the enumeration above is exhaustive for $n \le 1729$ (any representation of such an $n$ has $b \le 12$, and all such pairs were listed), and since $1729$ is the unique value below or equal to $1729$ that occurs twice, no smaller positive integer has two representations as a sum of two positive cubes.

---

## Conclusion

The smallest integer representable in two ways as a sum of two cubes is

$$\boxed{1729} = 1^3 + 12^3 = 9^3 + 10^3.$$
